I've kept your authentic founder voice ("partner in crime", budget realities) but tightened it to match the docs' existing tone.

## The ideas, organized

| # | Core idea | The point it makes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Why I built it** | I needed a "partner in crime" to develop my ideas. |
| 2 | **The reality** | The right talent at a budget price is hard to find — and that's normal. |
| 3 | **The drive** | I still have plenty of ideas to build, so codx-junior became that partner. |
| 4 | **The payoff** | A team to make ideas real and go live fast, at budget price. |
| 5 | **The safety net** | Freelancers can jump in when I'm stuck, without losing control — because codx-junior checks everything. |
| 6 | **The capability** | Multi-AI helps with brainstorming, design, images, coding, testing, deploying to cloud. |
| 7 | **The multiplier** | It also assists anyone who joins me. |

## Polished draft (ready to drop in)

```md
# Why I built codx-junior

I built codx-junior because I needed a partner in crime to help develop my ideas.

Finding the right talent at a price that works is hard — and that's normal. Good developers
are expensive, and a good idea shouldn't stall just because the budget is small. I still have
plenty of ideas I want to bring to life, so codx-junior became the partner I was looking for.

## A team at budget price

With codx-junior I have a team I can work with: we take an idea, make it real and go live
fast, at a budget price. It fills the roles that would normally take several hires.

## I never lose control

Some ideas push me past what I can do alone. When I get stuck, I can pay a freelancer to jump
in and fix it — without losing control of my project, because codx-junior reviews and checks
every change for me.

## One multi-AI, every step

The multi-AI in codx-junior works with me across the whole journey: brainstorming, design,
images, coding, testing and deploying to the cloud. And it assists anyone who joins me.
```

## Where it fits

This is a **mission / origin note**, so it doesn't belong buried in a feature page. Best options, in order:

1. **New page `guide/why-codx-junior.md`** — added to the sidebar next to *What is codx-junior?* and *Architecture* (both in `guide/` and `/` sidebars in `.vitepress/config.mts`). Cleanest fit; keeps `introduction.md` focused.
2. **A "Why we built it" section inside `guide/introduction.md`** — if you want it above the fold on the main guide entry.
3. **`team.md`** — if you'd rather frame it as the founding story behind the team.

My recommendation is **option 1**: a dedicated page keeps your personal voice distinct from the objective product description, and gives the "partner in crime" line room to breathe as a headline.

Want me to create `guide/why-codx-junior.md` with the draft above and wire it into both sidebars in `.vitepress/config.mts`? Say the word and I'll write the files.

New projects can be added in one of two ways:

- Clone a project from a Git repository
- Provide a full path to an existing folder

Review the **Project Settings** to configure options specific to the project.

To improve codx-junior’s understanding of your codebase, configure the **Knowledge Settings**.

Profiles define how codx-junior should interact with your project. You can create multiple profiles to:

- Enforce coding standards

- Guide change suggestions
